title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Life-Saving WASH Assistance to the Most Vulnerable IDP and Rural Communities in Qansaxdhere District to Address the Impact of Dry Conditions and Mitigate Displacement Risks.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe 2024–2025 Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) highlights alarming WASH-related gaps across Somalia, especially affecting IDPs and vulnerable host communities. Key findings show that 26% of households rely on unsafe drinking water sources, while 69% of IDPs and 51% of host communities lack adequate water for daily needs like drinking, cooking, and washing. A significant portion of the population, particularly 25% of IDPs, continues to depend on surface water, exposing them to waterborne diseases such as cholera and diarrhea.ltbrgtSanitation gaps are equally concerning. 58% of IDPs rely on shared latrines, while only 22% of household's overall use pit latrines, often in poor condition. This lack of safe, private, and accessible sanitation contributes to increased health and protection risks, especially for women, girls, and persons with disabilities. The combined impact of inadequate water access, poor sanitation, and limited hygiene awareness is driving a deteriorating public health situation and worsening community vulnerability.ltbrgtIn response to critical WASH gaps identified in the Qansaxdhere IDP settlements of Bay Region, KRDO proposes a lifesaving, integrated WASH intervention targeting 2083 households (12,500 individuals). This project aims to address both acute humanitarian needs and build resilience through sustainable, community-centered water, sanitation, and hygiene services.ltbrgtTo maximize impact, KRDO will integrate this WASH response with its active Health, Nutrition, Livelihood, and Protection programs and coordinate with key cluster partners including SAMA, ACTED, WASDA, GRRN, ACF, and others working in Qansaxdhere. This sectoral integration will enhance resource efficiency, reinforce public health outcomes, and ensure comprehensive service delivery to the most vulnerable.ltbrgtKey WASH activities include:ltbrgtSupport 10,000 people through rehabilitation of one strategic borehole, upgrading solar-powered pumping systems and installing improved water storage tanks.ltbrgtExtension of piped water networks to health centers, schools, and IDP settlements to increase equitable water access.ltbrgtEstablishment and training of 1 gender-balanced Water Management Committees in collaboration with communities, local authorities, and line ministries to ensure sustainability and community ownership.ltbrgtIn sanitation, KRDO will construct 75 emergency latrines, 15% of which will be disability-friendly, and each equipped with solar lighting for safety and GBV risk reduction.ltbrgtTo promote environmental health, 30 sanitation toolkits will be distributed to community sanitation groups, and conduct 24 solid waste management campaigns.ltbrgtFurthermore, KRDO will conduct 30 hygiene promotion sessions and facilitate the purchase and distribution of 1033 hygiene kits and training of hygiene promoters, project staff on PSEA, conduct post distribution monitoring and baseline assessment. ltbrgtThe intervention fully adheres to SPHERE Standards and Somalia WASH Cluster guidelines, with mainstreamed protection, disability inclusion, and gender sensitivity in line with the IASC GBV guidelines. Full community engagement and inclusive participation will be prioritized throughout project planning and implementation.ltbrgtThis intervention aims to deliver urgent WASH services while laying the foundation for long-term sustainability, resilience, and dignity for the displaced and host communities in Qansaxdhere.ltbrgtlt/pgt
